newsitem.title: INDIA: India Chidambaram lists January reforms as package.
newsitem.headline: India Chidambaram lists January reforms as package.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram released on Thursday a list of decisions taken this month by his government to spur the economy and said they amounted to a package of economic reforms.

"January has been an active, productive, fruitful month," Chidambaram told at a news conference at his New Delhi office. "I hope every month of this year is as fruitful." Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda had assured industrialists at a meeting last month his government was working on a package to revive sagging capital markets.
"Taken together, I believe, they constitute a cohesive package of decisions which will impart greater thrust to economic reforms," Chidambaram said in a statement.

"It is my hope that this compilation will help to appreciate better the determination of the government to continue the process of economic reforms in order to make the economy more efficient, more productive and more competitive," it said.

The list, including decisions taken on Thursday to allow foreign portfolio investment in debt and government gilts, was announced before Deve Gowda's scheduled visit with Chidambaram to Davos in Switzerland for the World Economic Forum's annual summit.
Deve Gowda had promised to reveal a package of measures before he left for Davos.
Many of the decisions taken this month related to encouragement of foreign investment in the infrastructure, wooed by India under a reform programme launched in 1991.
